title: Extending partial sections over a specified simplicial contraction
statement: Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products and pullbacks, standard simplices and horns as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $L$ be a simplicial set with a vertex $b$, and suppose a simplicial map $c:L\times\Delta^1\to L$ satisfies $c(-,0)=\operatorname{const}_b$ and $c(-,1)=\mathrm{id}_L$. Let $i:C\hookrightarrow L$ be a degreewise injective simplicial map. Let $q:E\to L$ be a Kan fibration, meaning that it lifts every horn inclusion $\Lambda_j^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$, $0\leq j\leq m$, and put $K=\{b\}\times_LE$. Suppose every simplicial map $u:C\to K$ extends to a simplicial map $v:L\to K$ with $vi=u$. Then every simplicial map $a:C\to E$ with $qa=i$ extends to a simplicial map $s:L\to E$ with $qs=\mathrm{id}_L$ and $si=a$. No Kan assumption on $L$ or $E$, no weak-equivalence assumption, and no requirement that $c$ fix $b$ at intermediate times is imposed.

source.place: Agent lemma extracted from step 4 of lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion: two corner-map path lifts and an intervening fiber extension, using SSet.fibration_pullbackObjObjπ, lines 70-93. This is a consequence of the source theorem, not its statement. No Stacks tag states this simplicial section-extension lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map] to the degreewise injection $\varnothing\hookrightarrow C$ and the given Kan fibration $q:E\to L$. Since $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,E)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,L)$ are one-point simplicial sets, its corner map identifies with the Kan fibration $q_C:\operatorname{Fun}(C,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(C,L)$ given by postcomposition. The formula $d=c\circ(i\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}):C\times\Delta^1\to L$ defines an edge of the target, by the internal-hom definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Its final endpoint is $i=qa$. Lift this edge through $q_C$ with prescribed final vertex $a$, using the horn $\Lambda^1_1=\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. The lifted edge is a map $A:C\times\Delta^1\to E$ with $qA=d$ and $A(-,1)=a$. Put $A_0=A(-,0)$. Then $qA_0=\operatorname{const}_b\circ i$, so pairing $A_0$ with the unique map $C\to\{b\}$ defines $u:C\to K=\{b\}\times_LE$ by the degreewise pullback formula.

source.place: SSet.fibration_pullbackObjObjπ, lines 70-93, specialized to the empty inclusion into C; agent dimension-one final-endpoint horn lift

proof.text: Use the assumed extension property on the map $u:C\to K$ from step 1 to choose $v:L\to K$ satisfying $vi=u$. Let $\widetilde v:L\to E$ be its composite with the pullback projection $K\to E$. The pullback identity gives $q\widetilde v=\operatorname{const}_b:L\to L$, and $vi=u$ gives $\widetilde v i=A_0$. These are equalities of simplicial maps, since the products and pullbacks in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] are degreewise.

source.place: Agent lemma, fiber-extension hypothesis in the statement

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map] to $i:C\hookrightarrow L$ itself and $q:E\to L$. Its Kan corner map is $r:\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)\to T$, where $T=\operatorname{Fun}(C,E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,L)}\operatorname{Fun}(L,L)$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $A$ is an edge of the first factor and $c$ an edge of the second. The identity $qA=c(i\times\mathrm{id})$ is precisely their compatibility in the pullback, so $(A,c)$ is an edge of $T$. Its initial vertex is $(A_0,\operatorname{const}_b)=r(\widetilde v)$ by step 2. Lift this edge through $r$ with prescribed initial vertex $\widetilde v$, using $\Lambda^1_0=\{0\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. The resulting edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)$ is $H:L\times\Delta^1\to E$ with $qH=c$ and $H(i\times\mathrm{id})=A$. Set $s=H(-,1)$. Evaluating the first equality at $1$ gives $qs=c(-,1)=\mathrm{id}_L$, and evaluating the second gives $si=A(-,1)=a$, as required.
